subject: reaction_eng
title: RTD Studies in a Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor
aim: To study the non-ideality of continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) and to find mean residence time for impulse injection of tracer; to plot exit age distribution (E curve) of the reactor.
apparatus: CSTR setup with stirrer motor and variable speed drive
Peristaltic feed pump & feed control valve
theory:
Non-ideality in reactors arises due to deviation from ideal flow patterns (plug flow and mixed flow), caused by channeling of fluid, recycling, or creation of stagnant regions. In CSTR, elements of fluid taking different routes through the reactor require different lengths of time to pass through the vessel.

The distribution of these times for the stream of liquid leaving the vessel is called the exit age distribution E or residence time distribution (RTD) of the fluid. With no tracer initially present anywhere, an idealized instantaneous pulse of tracer is imposed on the entering stream. The normalized response is then called the C curve or E curve.

Exit Age Distribution Function:
E(t) = C(t) / ∫₀^∞ C(t) dt ≈ C(t) / Σ (C(t) Δt)

Mean Residence Time:
t̄ = ∫₀^∞ t C(t) dt / ∫₀^∞ C(t) dt ≈ Σ (t C(t) Δt) / Σ (C(t) Δt)

For an ideal single CSTR:
E_theoretical(t) = (1 / t̄) * exp(-t / t̄)
procedure: Prepare 1 L of 0.1 N HCl and 100 mL of 1 N NaOH solutions.
Standardize NaOH solutions using standard oxalic acid (0.1 N) and standardize HCl using known normality of NaOH.
Open feed valve V3-V4 and fill the feed tank with water.
Start the supply of water to the reactor at a particular flow rate (e.g. 5 LPH).
Allow the experiment to reach steady state.
At time t=0, inject the tracer pulse of 10 mL (1 N NaOH) at the injection point in the mixed flow reactor and start the stopwatch.
Collect 10 mL of mixture from the outlet and transfer into a conical flask at regular time intervals (Δt = 30 sec).
Titrate the collected reaction mixture against standard HCl solution using phenolphthalein indicator until pale pink color disappears.
Tabulate observations, calculate C, CΔt, tCΔt, E, and mean residence time t̄.

python.label: Python (NumPy / SciPy) Reference
python.code:
import math

N_HCl = 1.0        # standardized HCl normality (N) — student-entered
Vol_sample = 10.0   # mL — student-entered
dt = 30.0            # sec — student-entered

trials = [
    {"t": 30,  "V3": 0.4},
    {"t": 60,  "V3": 0.6},
    {"t": 90,  "V3": 0.8},
    {"t": 120, "V3": 0.6},
    {"t": 150, "V3": 0.4},
    {"t": 180, "V3": 0.4},
    {"t": 210, "V3": 0.4},
]

for tr in trials:
    tr["C"] = tr["V3"] * N_HCl / Vol_sample
    tr["CDt"] = tr["C"] * dt

sum_CDt = sum(tr["CDt"] for tr in trials)

for tr in trials:
    tr["tCDt"] = tr["t"] * tr["CDt"]
    tr["E"] = tr["C"] / sum_CDt

sum_tCDt = sum(tr["tCDt"] for tr in trials)
t_bar = sum_tCDt / sum_CDt

for tr in trials:
    print(f"t={tr['t']:>3} s  C={tr['C']:.4f}  CDt={tr['CDt']:.3f}  " 
          f"E={tr['E']*1000:.3f}e-3  tCDt={tr['tCDt']:.1f}")

print(f"Sum CDt = {sum_CDt:.3f}, Sum tCDt = {sum_tCDt:.1f}")
print(f"Mean residence time = {t_bar:.2f} sec")
